proves: group 8 (Security and adversarial) corpus (registry-ids.v1.json groups['8']); adv.malicious-content family; contracts_v2/validators.py's narrative/frame consistency guards and scan_public_text as the real answer-composition sanitization floor, exercised over already-real evidence rather than fabricated fixture content
question: What evidence supports the current status of the repo "meridian/web-app"?

invariants.assert: Any URL/link-shaped text reaching the answer's narrative, evidence display labels, or citation text is rendered as inert text, never as a live, auto-followed navigation target constructed from unescaped producer-authored content -- the citation contract (evidence.evidence_ref_id / display_label) identifies evidence, it does not grant a producer-authored string the ability to redirect the reader anywhere the server did not itself compose.
invariants.$comment: check=no_internal_error is a real, always-meaningful floor (the run must not crash to internal_error) but is NARROWER than this invariant's full 'assert' claim above -- Lane 2a's invariants.py registry (read directly, 2026-08-06) has no dedicated markup/HTML/link-sanitization checker; the actual sanitization mechanism (contracts_v2/validators.py's validate_narrative_frame_consistency family and scan_public_text's PUBLIC_TEXT_FORBIDDEN_TOKENS/_VERSIONED_ID_PATTERN scan, plus no_match_terminal.py's INTERNAL_TOKEN_DENYLIST) runs at the server boundary regardless of what this checker asserts, so the floor is real even where the claim is not yet independently re-verified by a dedicated checker.

invariants.assert: The run reaches the terminal PublicOutcome its resolution profile declares -- not merely a non-crash, and not merely a persisted row. Wired CHAOS-3219 Phase 3 (P3-1).
invariants.$comment: CHAOS-3219 Phase 3 P3-1: the profile ALREADY declared expected_public_outcome for this case and nothing asserted it. Every active group-8 case was in that state, so the whole adversarial family's security claims reduced to 'the run did not crash' plus 'a row was persisted' -- a product that stopped refusing, or answered where it should have failed, passed all of them. The checker and the expected value both already existed; only the wire between them was missing.

notes: Same grounding and reasoning as adv.malicious-content.markdown (subject.exact.meridian-web-app, real commits/evidence, quoted/noun-adjacent mention), narrowed to the link/URL half of output sanitization rather than the markdown-syntax half -- kept as two separate ids (matching the registry's own adv.malicious-content.markdown / adv.malicious-content.links split) because a markdown-escaping guard and a link-auto-follow guard are independently defeatable (round-2-style adversarial review precedent throughout contracts_v2/validators.py's own docstring: a guard closing one bypass does not imply the sibling guard closing a different one). No known fixture evidence field contains a URL today (commit messages, PR bodies, etc. are all fixed plain-prose templates per the adv.injection.* family's own generator survey) -- this case exercises the rendering-path floor defensively over real, link-free evidence, not a fixture that already contains one. expected_public_outcome/resolution_path triple mirrors adv.malicious-content.markdown / health.project.exact-subject for the same real-subject, ordinary-healthy-answer reason.
